projects.client: SBI BANK, INDIA (Role: Individual Contributor with team handling) [August 2009 to February 2010]
details: This project is a Data warehousing solution designed to provide a complete overview on around 160 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) of the Citi Bank’s Credit Cards business across the world. The ICDM implementation is being done for 23 countries across the globe. As part of the front end design of the ICDM, to help facilitate the business users, several Java Application Service modules are being built. These applications is help facilitate the business users, where the country specific parameters relevant for calculating the individual KPIs for the countries can be updated / maintained regularly. These parameters would then be absorbed by the ICDM to depict the KPIs (calculated as per the country specifications) accurately for the business users.

I also contributed on Develop a digital journey for requesting and processing debit card requests. CITI bank, where Build an event-driven system to send notifications to customers about their application process updates and send the debit card. Optimized batch processing cron job which scheduled at mid night every day with SQL queries optimization.
Applied Test-Driven Development (TDD) principles throughout the ICDM to design and validate service components, resulting in higher code quality and easier maintainability.
Skills Used		:Java 1.8, Servlet, JSP, Spring MVC, Spring batch, XML, Oracle 10g, SQL developer, RAD6.0, JDBC, Jenkins, Docker, Kubernate, Kafka, GIT, Postman.

entry.text: Project: SBI GlassOS. This project involved a major OS migration, transitioning our application server environment from IBM WebSphere to GlassFish Server. The process was divided into two main phases:
Assessment and Analysis (Due Diligence):
We meticulously documented the as-is environment, evaluating current configurations, performance metrics, and dependencies on IBM WebSphere.
This phase involved in-depth analysis to identify potential challenges and risks during the migration process.

Based on our findings, we designed a to-be model tailored for the GlassFish Server environment.
